- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (true > 70.0), model often overreacts and overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +1.0% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) mid-horizon, model frequently fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day windows; if forecast is > 1.5% above 30d moving average, reduce by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral (±0.1) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; use 30d EWMA instead of raw forecast for smoothing.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by > 2.0% for 3+ consecutive days, model is lagging; add 0.5–1.0% to next forecast to catch up.
